newsitem.title: USA: USG wallboard, ceiling demand rises.
newsitem.headline: USG wallboard, ceiling demand rises.

text.p: USG Corp said strong construction activity led to record demand for its gypsum wallboard and suspended ceilings in the third quarter.
USG said it realized price increases on wallboard, ceiling tile and ceiling suspension grid during the quarter. Wallboard prices rose $8 per thousand square foot in late September.

"We are optimistic that the U.S. construction market will continue to benefit from ongoing moderate economic growth, relatively low inflation, high consumer confidence, solid repair and remodel growth and good home affordability," William Foote, chairman, said in a statement.
"Asian and Latin American market conditions are expected to remain favorable, while Canada and Europe continue to show signs of a gradual economic recovery."

USG said its North American gypsum business recorded net sales of $543 million, up 11 percent, and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amoritzation (EBITDA) of $115 million, up 21 percent.

United States Gypsum Co's wallboard plants ran at 97 percent of capacity in the third quarter. Its average selling price for gypsum wallboard of $112.08 per thousand square feet was about five percent higher than in the preceding quarter.
The gypsum wallboard price was also two percent higher than in the third quarter of 1995.

The company's third-quarter shipments of gypsum wallboard totaled 2.10 billion square feet, about seven percent above third-quarter 1995 shipments of 1.96 billion square feet and a record for any quarter in the company's history.
USG's worldwide ceilings business recorded net sales of $158 million, compared with $161 million in the third quarter of 1995. EBITDA of $20 million was five percent above the prior-year period.
Earlier, USG reported third quarter earnings of $0.26 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.04.

To make progress toward its goal of an investment grade rating, USG said it reduced the principal amount of its debt by an additional $69 million during the third quarter. As of September 30, debt totaled $795 million, a reduction of $131 million during the first nine months of 1996.

USG said its third quarter interest expense declined $7 million, or 28 percent, compared with the third quarter of 1995, primarily reflecting a lower level of debt in 1996. -- Reuters Chicago Newsdesk - 312-408-8787
